symptom: create javascript action with a $$ body indented one tab throughout wrote every line after the first with one extra tab (file tabs 1,3,4,3,3 for a 1,2,3,2,2 body); describe printed the extra tab back, so each describe → exec shifted the code right.
cause: The visitor TrimSpace'd the body, which removes only the FIRST line's leading whitespace; GenerateJavaScriptSource then prefixes every line with a tab; the JS describe reader kept the stored indentation (Java's reader dedented via normalizeJavaSection, JS's did not).
fix: codesection.Normalize (LF, edge blank lines dropped, common indentation removed, trailing whitespace trimmed) is the one rule: the visitor applies it to Java and JavaScript bodies, and both describe readers use it.
insight: A writer that indents uniformly needs a RELATIVE body on both of its inputs — what the parser hands it and what describe reads back. TrimSpace looks like normalisation but is first-line-only for indentation. Java had already learned this on the describe side only, so Java hand-written indented bodies had the same latent shift.
test: mdl/executor/js_action_body_indent_2131_test.go (tabs as written; describe → exec fixed point; control: flush-left bodies unchanged); reverted: tabs [1 3 4 3 3]
